result.title: ASCG: Adaptive Spatial Classifier Guidance for Surgical Concept Suppression in Diffusion Models
result.comment: 9 pages, including references and supplementary material
result.summary: While text-to-image (T2I) diffusion models achieve remarkable quality, they risk producing harmful content. Existing safety mechanisms often rely on indiscriminate, global interventions that induce unintended semantic drift and degrade image quality. To address this, we propose Adaptive Spatial Classifier Guidance (ASCG), a necessity-driven framework that employs probabilistic monitoring to activate guidance selectively upon harm detection. By leveraging Grad-CAM for localized suppression, ASCG effectively removes harmful concepts while preserving superior semantic fidelity compared to conventional methods. Furthermore, we overcome the limitations of traditional metrics like NudeNet---which fails to assess semantic integrity---by introducing a VLM-based evaluation framework to provide a fine-grained, robust analysis of both safety and context preservation. Our results demonstrate that ASCG not only balances safety and fidelity but also exhibits remarkable plug-and-play synergy with existing frameworks to establish state-of-the-art performance.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 ASCG，用概率监测在检测到有害内容时才触发引导，并借助 Grad-CAM 做局部概念抑制，同时引入 VLM 评估框架以同时衡量安全性与语义保真度。
AI.relevance_reason: 其核心是「由监测信号决定何时介入、并在何处施加局部干预」，与 latent reasoning 中基于置信度/证据触发额外计算或停止的决策、以及定位视觉证据位置的思路存在可核查的形式类比；但研究对象是图像生成安全，是否可迁移需读原文判断。
